subject: maths
title: Primary 3 Adding and Subtracting Fractions
seo_title: P3 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets: Free Primary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Adding and subtracting two related fractions within one whole (denominators not exceeding 12)
meta_desc: Free P3 maths practice: add and subtract like and related fractions within one whole, simplest form and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Make the denominators the same, then add or subtract only the numerators.
body_html:
Like fractions: add or subtract the numerators

When the denominators are the same, the parts are the same size. Add or subtract the numerators. The denominator does not change.

Example

27 + 37 = ?

Add the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5. Keep the denominator 7.

Answer: 57

Example

79 − 39 = ?

Subtract the numerators: 7 − 3 = 4. Keep the denominator 9.

Answer: 49

Related fractions: make the denominators the same

Halves and quarters are different sizes, so you cannot add them as they are. 4 is a multiple of 2, so change 12 into quarters. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number.

Example

12 + 14 = ?

2 × 2 = 4, so 12 = 24. Then 24 + 14 = 34.

Answer: 34

Example

23 − 16 = ?

3 × 2 = 6, so 23 = 46. Then 46 − 16 = 36 = 12.

Answer: 12

Give the answer in simplest form

Divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number until you cannot divide any more.

CalculationWorkingSimplest form
18 + 5868 (6 and 8 ÷ 2)34
13 + 1626 + 16 = 36 (3 and 6 ÷ 3)12
910 − 12910 − 510 = 410 (4 and 10 ÷ 2)25

Subtracting from 1

Write 1 whole as a fraction with the same denominator, such as 1 = 88.

Word problems: draw a model

Draw a bar for the whole. Mark the parts you know and put “?” on the part you need to find. Then decide whether to add or subtract.

Example

Ali ate 18 of a cake. Siti ate 12 of the cake. What fraction of the cake was left?

Eaten: 18 + 48 = 58. Left: 88 − 58 = 38.

Answer: 38

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
27 + 37 = 514 (adding the denominators)Keep the denominator: 57
12 + 14 = 24 (not changing to the same denominator)Change 12 to 24 first: 24 + 14 = 34
18 + 58 = 68 (answer not simplified)Divide by 2: 34
1 − 38 = 28 (taking 1 from the numerator)Write 1 as 88: 88 − 38 = 58

faq.q: What is taught in P3 adding and subtracting fractions?
faq.a: In Primary 3, students add and subtract two related fractions within one whole, with denominators up to 12, such as 1/2 + 1/4 or 2/3 − 1/6. They give the answer in simplest form.

faq.q: How do I explain adding fractions with different denominators to my child?
faq.a: Make the parts the same size first. For 1/2 + 1/4, fold a paper strip to show that 1/2 = 2/4, then add: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when adding fractions?
faq.a: Adding the denominators, as in 1/5 + 3/5 = 4/10. The parts are still fifths, so the answer is 4/5.

faq.q: Is adding and subtracting fractions in the MOE syllabus for Primary 3?
faq.a: Yes. It is part of Fractions in the Primary 3 Standard Mathematics syllabus (MOE 2021). In Primary 4, students go on to answers greater than 1 and mixed numbers.

items.q:
Hui Min has read 512 of her library book. What fraction of the book has she not read yet?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The whole book is 1. Not read = 1 − read. Write 1 whole as 1212. Then 1212 − 512 = 712. The answer is 712.

items.q:
A fish tank was 1112 full of water. Mr Kumar let out some water to clean it. Then the tank was 13 full. What fraction of the tank did he let out?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Water let out = before − after. 12 is a multiple of 3, so change both fractions into twelfths. Multiply the numerator and denominator by 4: 13 = 412. Subtract the numerators: 1112 − 412 = 712. The answer is 712.
